payload.detail: finger_joint effort exceeded max_clamp_effort while holding u_brown

payload.reason: scene_watch_1 observation fire during pick_u_brown; checking for unexpected objects/intrusions vs expected arm motion

payload.explanation: get_evidence on joint_states/finger_joint across trigger_wall_ns=1792614756699021000 shows effort ramping smoothly from ~-0.02 up through 5.6, 11.76 (first threshold crossing), 19.0, 27.4, 35.2... and plateauing at a steady ~58.74 sim_effort while finger_joint position holds flat at 0.6329 (fully closed on the part). This is a clean, monotonic grasp-closure effort curve with no noise or double-bump, consistent with the gripper fingers closing fully onto u_brown and continuing to apply clamping force well past contact rather than backing off once contact was made. u_brown's registry max_clamp_effort is 10 (raw_spec.limits.max_clamp_effort), so the sustained plateau at ~58.74 is roughly 5.9x the part's tolerated clamp effort -- this is an overforceful grasp, not sensor noise or a momentary spike, since it held steady for the remainder of the evidence window. I did not flag the concurrent scene_watch_1 observation fire (mean depth change 0.0318 vs agent-chosen 0.03 trigger): look() at the same time shows only the arm/gripper over the bench mid-pick, matching the expected motion for this step, no unidentified object or bystander disturbance, so it is not a requirement violation.

payload.explanation:
This is the run's final end-state verdict, covering pick_u_brown through place_inverted_u_yellow (steps_covered). I measured each part's final pose against its own placement frame via query_snapshot at run end: u_brown 0.00259m, u_orange 0.0021m, line_green 0.0065m, inverted_u_yellow 0.00141m from their respective placement frames -- all within each part's position_m tolerance (0.01/0.02/0.015/0.012 respectively), closely matching the executor's own claimed position errors. All five bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2) sit within ~0.03mm of their run-start reference poses -- effectively unmoved -- and base1 drifted a cumulative 0.0075m from its start pose, under the 0.02m disturbance tolerance; none of my 9 stationarity monitors ever fired. Each part's effects clauses (lift height, tcp-offset/no-slip, grasp-effort-plateau-floor, grasp-width-error) were verified from get_evidence/monitor evidence at or after each part's own place-step close, all passing.

The one finding on the timeline: during pick_u_brown, clamp_effort_u_brown fired at 11.76 sim_effort and get_evidence showed the finger_joint effort plateauing at a steady ~58.74, versus u_brown's registry max_clamp_effort of 10 -- a real overforceful grasp (invariants.grasp_effort_instantaneous), recorded as non_conformant under step pick_u_brown. This is the case where the executor's own run_ended claim ("all clamp efforts well under registry limits") directly contradicts my physical evidence for u_brown. However this breach was transient to the grasp phase and left no lasting defect: u_brown tracked the gripper rigidly afterward (slip monitor never fired) and was ultimately seated within tolerance, so the run recovered from this finding rather than ending with any violation still standing.

Process notes, not violations: end_step for place_u_orange was never published before begin_step pick_line_green started (it arrived late, after pick_line_green had already begun) -- I independently verified u_orange's seating and u_brown's non-disturbance from query_snapshot/get_evidence at the time, and the delayed end_step's claimed values (position_error 0.00254m, u_brown_disturbance 0.00261m) matched my own evidence closely. No step outside the expected process occurred; the plan's 12 listed steps covered the whole run.

Conclusion: every part's final pose meets its placement frame within tolerance, every bystander and base1 stayed within the disturbance tolerance, and the one standing finding (pick_u_brown clamp-effort) did not leave any uncorrected defect in the end-state, so this run is conformant with recovery from that one mid-run finding.
